answer: Before any reward claim, each identity must lock a refundable stake and pass randomly timed audits; proof that accounts share one controller burns the linked stakes. An attacker creating 100 identities therefore immobilizes 100 deposits and risks losing all 100, while an honest identity gets its stake back after its audit voyage. Random challenge labels such as raven and meadow make copied responses detectable, rather than letting one operator reuse a single proof. A voyage requires its own stake.
